adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new fallback paths that fetch a credential record directly by `id` from the DB without any ownership/authorization validation. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, if `destination.credentialId` is set but not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, it does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } ... })` and then uses that credential to call `createEvent(...)`. Similarly in `EventManager`’s update flow (processing `calendarReference`), if a reference has `credentialId` but it’s not in `this.calendarCredentials`, it fetches it from DB by ID and proceeds to `updateEvent(...)`. In `handleCancelBooking`, if `credentialId` isn’t found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, it fetches it by ID (`prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })`) and then uses it to delete calendar events. The diff shows no checks like `where: { id, userId: bookingToDelete.userId }` / team membership / org scoping before using the OAuth keys, so if an attacker can influence `credentialId` in `destinationCalendar` or booking references, this enables IDOR-style abuse/cross-account calendar operations.
